thread.title: Will New Hearing Aid Laws Affect Amplifon? - Amplifon S.p.A. (OTCMKTS:AMFPF)

author: Holmes Osborne
title: Will New Hearing Aid Laws Affect Amplifon? - Amplifon S.p.A. (OTCMKTS:AMFPF)
text:
Last August, Congress passed a law allowing the sale of over-the-counter hearing aids. Presently, buyers need to go to an audiologist which adds to the cost. Italy-based Amplifon ( OTC:AMFPF , OTC:AMFPY ), which controls 10% of the market and owns Miracle-Ear, has put up fantastic growth numbers and has been extremely profitable. The stock is very expensive, and my guess is that it will be affected by the new law as it's phased in. The moat that has been protecting the hearing aid industry is being partially taken down.
In August of last year, Congress passed legislation that allowed people to buy hearing aids without the assistance of a licensed audiologist. Approximately 80 million Americans suffer from hearing loss and many people could not afford hearing aids as they average $2,300 in cost. Many medical plans do not cover hearing aids as they are viewed as elective. Nancy Macklin , director of external affairs for the Hearing Loss Association of America, estimates that over-the-counter hearing aids could cost as little as $500. The bill faced opposition from six largest hearing aid manufacturers that control 90% of the market.
Amplifon's stock trades for €17.43, it has 219 million shares, and its market cap is €3.8 billion ($4.4 billion). Earnings were €.46 and the price to earnings ratio is 38. Not a cheap stock. The dividend is €.11, and the dividend yield is 0.6%.
The company grew sales from €830 million ($963 million) in 2013 to €1.27 billion ($1.47 billion) in 2017. That's growth! Earnings per share grew from €.06 to €.45 over that time frame. Return on equity was 18.32% and the net income was 8%. Net income margins that high are few and far between.
The balance sheet shows €101 million in cash and €189 million in receivables. The liability side shows €127 million in payables and €548 million in debt. Not bad. Last year, the company put up €118 million in free cash flow. That's a 3.1% free cash flow yield. Again, a little pricey.
Amplifon receives 67.6% of sales from Europe/Middle East/Africa, 18.1% the Americas, and 14.1% Asia. It has 4,300 points of sales across the globe. Its stores and brands include: Amplifon, Beter Horen, Maxtone, and Miracle-Ear.
I found an ad on the internet for NANO , "Hearing aids without the middleman". You can get a pair of hearing aids for $249. Hearingdirect.com has an abundance of reasonably priced hearing aids. Many users will be able to access these websites for hearing needs, thus, cutting into Amplifon's profits.
I was curious to see if the new laws have affected Amplifon yet. Nope. In the first quarter, sales growth was 9.7%. Organic growth was 5.4%. Sales growth in the Americas was 3.6%. The company had an Investor Presentation back in March. Nowhere in its 63-page slide presentation do I see where anything is mentioned about the new U.S. laws. An article in the New York Times states that the FDA is going to phase over-the-counter hearing aids over three years. An article from Kaiser opines that the reason hearing aids are so expensive is because of the services that come with them.
I was also curious to see if Europeans needed an audiologist to buy a hearing aid. Europeans do indeed need audiologist, and the audiologists are fighting for changes in Europe too. Thus far, the laws have not changed which is good for Amplifon.
Apple ( AAPL ) has ways of matching up its iPhones with hearing aids. I've seen people answer their phones and chat with the help of their hearing aids. Many people think that Apple will compete against the major hearing aid manufacturers like Amplifon.
There are two reasons I wrote this article. The first is that Amplifon is a great company that gets little attention in the U.S. I found it by perusing Oakmark International Small Cap's holdings. The second reason is that I was curious to learn about the new law affecting the hearing aid industry. I wouldn't buy the stock because of its high price. I also wouldn't buy as the new law could cut into sales in the U.S. Having stated this, Amplifon may just shrug off over-the-counter issues and continue selling high-end hearing aids to the Baby Boomer generation.
